title: Keep tmux from stamping backgrounds on self-reloading terminals
head: 0f760706edb7

leads.summary: Skip path erases application-owned pane palettes even when Omarchy has never stamped that pane
leads.consequence: With an attached ghostty or kitty tmux client, every theme change sends OSC 104, 110 and 111 to every pane before it checks whether either global style has an Omarchy record. A program in an otherwise untouched pane that set an OSC 4 palette (or OSC 10/11 defaults) loses those per-pane choices. This changes its displayed ANSI colours and default colours, even if the user's global window-style was changed or no Omarchy stamp exists. It also clears 16-255 entries not emitted by omarchy-theme-osc. The window-style equality guard cannot protect this output. Consider tracking and comparing Omarchy's own pane palette/default-colour writes before resetting them, or otherwise limiting the unconditional reset to panes known to have been stamped.

prior_findings.claim: Earlier stamps (global window-style/window-active-style and per-pane OSC colours from upgrade, detached or non-matching-client runs) survive the skip path, so panes show the previous theme.
prior_findings.reason: Resolved for stamps written by the current head (detached and foot-only runs are recorded in @omarchy_* and cleared by the next ghostty/kitty change; verified in private tmux 3.7c). comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13132#issuecomment-5824377612) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13132#issuecomment-5826625565), checked at `0f760706`.

**Verified:** stamps that the current script writes are now cleared. A theme change made while tmux is detached, or with only a foot-like (`xterm-256color`) client attached, records its stamp in `@omarchy_*`. The next change made from ghostty then unsets `window-style`/`window-active-style`, resets pane foreground and background to default (including a pane created after the stamp), and tmux sends default-colour cells (SGR 49) again. A `window-style` set in `tmux.conf` that differs from the record is left alone. The any-client rule is now stated in the function comment, which addresses the second finding. The alacritty scope explanation is accurate: its `TERM` is the same as foot's.

The stale-stamp finding is resolved for stamps the new script writes, and still present in two narrower forms: stamps written before the update, and the per-pane cursor colour.

| Sequence (private tmux 3.7c, synthetic themes A, B, C, ghostty pty client) | Previously reviewed head | Current head |
|---|---|---|
| Theme A set while detached, new pane split, ghostty attaches, then B | `window-style` A, panes A | `window-style` default, panes default; cursor of the first pane still A |
| Theme A set by the pre-PR script (still-running server after the update), then B, then C | panes A (earlier review) | `window-style` still A, panes still A bg and fg after both B and C |
| foot-like client sets A, ghostty joins, then B | not run | `window-style` default, panes default; cursor still A |

### Stamps written before the update are not cleared

`clear_tmux_window_style` unsets a style only when it matches its `@omarchy_*` record (`bin/omarchy-theme-set-tmux:95-97`). The pre-PR script never wrote a record, so `show-option -gv @omarchy_window_style` fails and the loop continues without unsetting. On a tmux server that was stamped before the update and is still running, later theme changes from ghostty or kitty leave every pane on the pre-update theme's background and text colour, as in the second table row, until the restamp described under Impact. The comments at `bin/omarchy-theme-set-tmux:119-121` and `test/cli:607` state that the "before the upgrade" case is covered.

**Impact:** transitional, limited to one server lifetime per user. It lasts until tmux restarts, or until a theme change runs with no client or only a foot/alacritty client attached (that run restamps with a record, and the next ghostty/kitty change clears it). For those users it is worse than the base, which at least shows the new theme's colours.

**Suggested change:** a one-time migration that records the current global styles as `@omarchy_window_style`/`@omarchy_window_active_style` when they equal `fg=<current theme foreground>,bg=<current theme background>`. A sketch of that check, run in the same private tmux test (not as an Omarchy migration), let the next run of the current script clear the styles. A user-set style that differs from that exact value is left alone. Alternatively, keep the limit, tell users to restart tmux after updating, and drop "before the upgrade" from both comments.

### Stamped cursor colour survives the clear

Every stamping run also pushes the cursor colour (`OSC 12`, `bin/omarchy-theme-osc:26`) into each pane. In tmux 3.7c a pane's own cursor colour takes precedence over the `cursor-colour` option (`tty.c:772-776`). The reset string at `bin/omarchy-theme-set-tmux:90` sends `OSC 104`, `110` and `111` but not `OSC 112`, so panes that were stamped keep the previous theme's cursor colour after the styles are cleared, and tmux sends it to ghostty and foot clients (first and third table rows). Panes that were never stamped follow the new `cursor-colour`.

**Impact:** cosmetic. The cursor stays on an earlier theme's colour in those panes until they close or an application in them sends `OSC 112`.

**Suggested change:** add `\033]112\007` to the reset string (and to the source assert at `test/cli:629`). A diagnostic copy of the script with that change gave both panes the new cursor colour in the same test.

### The pane reset now also clears palette entries 16-255 set by applications

The argumentless `OSC 104` in the reset string clears the pane's whole palette, while the base push only ever overwrote entries 0-15. On any theme change made with ghostty or kitty attached, including on a never-stamped server, palette entries 16-255 that an application set with `OSC 4` inside a pane now fall back to the terminal's own colours. Reproduced in the private tmux test; with the base push those entries were kept.

**Impact:** minor and recoverable. It only affects tools that set those entries directly inside a pane (for example pywal, which writes entry 232), until the tool applies them again.

**Suggested change:** reset only entries 0-15 (`OSC 104;0;1;…;15`), then send `110`/`111`/`112`. That matches the base push's scope. The indexed form is accepted by tmux 3.7c's parser but was not run.

**Unchanged by design:** after a theme change made while detached, the next ghostty or kitty attach still shows opaque panes (in the correct colours) until the next theme change made with that terminal attached, as before this commit.

**Optional test improvement:** the pane-reset test only greps the script for the byte string, and none of the clear tests set `TMUX_TEST_PANE_TTY`, so the reset loop never runs under the mock. A clear test with the `TMUX_SHOW_omarchy_*` values left unset shows the pre-update gap above: it fails on the current head.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the current head, the previously reviewed head and the merge-base, plus tmux 3.7c, ghostty 1.3.1, kitty 0.49.1 and alacritty 0.17.0 source at the versions Arch ships. The head's `test/cli` was run in a sandbox against each tree: all tmux asserts pass on the current head, and on the previously reviewed head and the merge-base it stops at a tmux assert. A private tmux 3.7c server with Omarchy's `tmux.conf`, pty clients using `xterm-ghostty` and `xterm-256color`, and synthetic themes recorded tmux options, pane colours, cursor colours and the bytes tmux sent to a newly attached client. kitty was not exercised in that test (it takes the same code path). No GUI terminal was run, so on-screen rendering was not observed.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
